slides.texte_overlay:
psychology facts that
explain everyday behaviour

the halo effect

when someone is good at one thing, we assume they're good at everything. knowing this helps you judge people more fairly and look past first impressions.

the favour effect

when someone does us a small kindness, we feel a strong urge to return it. little kind gestures build far more goodwill than big, impressive ones ever do.

the curiosity effect

we see curious people as warmer, which is why learning a little every day changes how others react to you. curiosity is one of the warmest traits a person can show.
slides.texte_sophia:
the curiosity effect

we see curious people as warmer. i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, a planet or a painting, and people respond to me with so much more warmth now.

slides.texte_overlay:
the familiarity effect

we tend to like what we see often. that's why a face you pass every morning slowly starts to feel friendly, even if you've never spoken a single word.

the spotlight effect

people notice your small mistakes far less than you think. everyone is busy worrying about their own spotlight, so you can relax a little and let it go.
